content_text: something I'd add to this, in all scenarios like the ones mentioned (didn't get return offer, got fired, etc) 1/4 “Never lead with it, never minimize it” is advice I was given at some point which should keep you on the level...meaning you don't want to just launch directly into some manicured story of "why I got fired" primarily due to that people tend to draw their own conclusions on this stuff in advance, and/or do their own due diligence. but I've found with pretty much all mistakes and accountability, people will usually ask "what happened" -- despite already knowing the answer -- just to observe how you answer the question. because people fuck this up, all the time, in a seemingly infinite amount of ways blaming others, shitting on former coworkers/bosses, making excuses...offering some story where it just wasn't their fault, hoping to paint themselves in a good light 2/4 that never works, it always backfires I would even argue that its axiomatic where the "higher up" the person is, the more that brutal self-censure and 100% accountability will work in your favor. "will this person readily admit when they're wrong," holds more weight than any individual wrong, of which you will make thousands in your life so you may as well tell it straight...if only because over hundreds, if not thousands of these situations, you learn that what matters most is being able to get in bed that night and say "I gave it my absolute fucking all"... because beyond that, u really have no control. 3/4 nor is this just 21-year-old shit, like, you may have heard that something like 90% of businesses fail. yet you never hear a peep about any of this stuff...seems to magically get swept under the rug behind closed doors though, people will always get asked "what happened," if only to measure your character, to observe whether you take accountability when you're wrong, and so on. point being these scenarios and how u handle them, are a lifelong thing 4/4 beyond that, I'm at a loss as far as next steps. I can't think of anyone to point to who does an exceptional job of this, and say "mimic their approach," and have reservations over whether that would be wise in the first place / would come off as inauthentic or borrowed like most things in life, this is probably something you learn less through study, and more thru making humiliating fucking errors, thru pain, thru shame, and thru failure...same schoolteachers as always, and the only ones who administer lessons that stick.
